Situation1: A serious situation has come up in the family, and the grandparent's presence is needed.
Expectation2: Complete assigned tasks by the agreed deadlines
Situation2: The task sits on the critical path for an external delivery promised to a client.
Story: I stared at my phone, my daughter’s message still glowing on the screen: “Grandpa, can you come? We really need you.” My heart clenched. There was trouble at home—my son-in-law had been rushed to the hospital, and my daughter was overwhelmed. I knew my grandchildren would be scared, needing comfort and reassurance only I could give. But as I reached for my car keys, my work laptop chimed. An urgent email from my project manager: “We need your section of the report by tonight. The client is waiting, and everything else depends on your part.” I could almost hear the tension in her words. I was the linchpin, the one holding up the next phase. My team was counting on me, and missing this deadline could jeopardize the whole project. I felt torn in two—my family needed me, but so did my colleagues. The weight of both expectations pressed down, and I stood frozen, keys in one hand, laptop in the other, my mind racing and my heart aching, unsure which world to let down.
